comments.body:
## Phase 1 RCA — completion-verifier faults verdict-less on epic-close transport read-timeout

**Investigation:** 4 parallel investigators (code-tracer, historical, empirical runtime, pydantic-ai OSS lens). They **converge** on a single mechanism with an aggravating condition. Legitimacy: **`defect`** (resilience/bounding gap — cited below). Not a shared-store/contention issue.

### Proven root cause (parsimonious — one defect + one aggravating condition)

The completion-verifier's `CompletionAgentStep.run` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:100-113`) routes into the banked/deterministic recovery **only** three *typed output/budget* exhaustion exceptions — `LLMBudgetExhaustedError`, `RunawayToolLoopError`, `UnretryableOutputError` (token exhaustion). A **transport-availability failure** matches none of them.

On the epic-close finalize step (`gates/completion-verification.yaml` `decide.then.verify`, `output_budget: model_max`), the single large `converse` call read-times-out. Its finite provider retries exhaust — botocore `max_attempts=4 × read_timeout=600s` on the Bedrock path (`bedrock_model.py:171-174`), or tenacity `stop_after_attempt(4) × httpx.Timeout(600)` on the Anthropic path — and the failure is wrapped as **`LLMUnavailableError`** at `run_failure.py:202`.

`LLMUnavailableError(LLMError)` is a **sibling** of the caught `LLMRunnerError` subclasses (`errors.py:11,15,29,33,70`), so it is provably **not** caught by `run()`'s three `except` arms. It propagates past recovery to `completion_failures.py:232`, which raises the verdict-less `LLMError("completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict: …")`. **The gate faults instead of degrading to a verdict.**

- **Defect (the changeable artifact):** the missing transport-availability recovery arm at `completion_recovery.py:100-113` — an exhausted-provider `LLMUnavailableError` is never routed to the deterministic no-LLM finalizer.
- **Aggravating condition (why the timeout occurs at all):** the epic finalize call is large — the PRIMARY step budget is scaled up by direct-child count (`completion.py:233-236`) and the finalize runs at `output_budget=model_max` — so the single `converse` reliably exceeds the 600s read timeout. (Note: the close path uses `graph=False` at `close_autoresume.py:237`, so this is *not* descendant-subtree concatenation; it is step-budget-scaled agent history.)

### Proof (discriminating experiments + runtime oracle)

- **Retry engages (disproves rival A "retry not applied").** Empirical dynamic probe: a `MockTransport` raising `ReadTimeout` on every call drove **4** transport attempts (backoff 1s/2s/4s) then re-raised. `interpret_failure(wrapped ReadTimeout)` → **`LLMUnavailableError`** (runtime-observed), which is not one of the three recovery-catchable types.
- **Wall-clock arithmetic matches (supports B).** `4 × 600s (+backoff) = 2407s ≈ 40.1 min` — an exact match to the deterministic ~40 min, 3/3-identical reproduction.
- **Deterministic, not transient infra (disproves rival D).** 3/3 identical ~40 min faults are structural (a large call that always exceeds 600s), not a variable infra blip. The class hierarchy makes the propagation deterministic.
- **Timeout-too-low (rival C) is an aggravating/mitigating factor, not the cause** — even a higher timeout would still fault verdict-less, because the timeout bypasses recovery.

### Authoritative intended-behavior source (clears the not-a-bug guard → `defect`)

`completion_recovery.py:11-12` (module docstring): *"…a deterministic no-LLM fallback so a run with any banked progress can never die verdict-less."* The banked-recovery design (epics 10ae / 2948) exists precisely so the gate **degrades to a verdict rather than faults**. The transport-timeout path violates that invariant. Severity is **availability, not correctness** — it fails closed (no false PASS), it just fails *verdict-less* instead of degrading to an actionable BLOCK/FAIL.

Independent OSS corroboration (pydantic-ai lens, P0): the idiomatic fix across every resilience pattern is to **catch the provider fault and emit an explicit degrade verdict** rather than let it propagate as a fault. (It also flags that a pure Bedrock-Converse path raises botocore `ReadTimeoutError`, not `httpx.ReadTimeout` — so the dossier's `failure.py:271` httpx `WAIT_AND_RETRY` arm is the wrong transport; but classification is advisory metadata only — nothing re-runs the decide step on it — so the fix is at the recovery-routing layer, not classification.)

### Defect attribution (`caused_by`)

**`caused_by = d2ce-36f5-fd08-4e40`** — commit `5bc3a432d7` "d2ce: default local dev to Bedrock" (epic 061c seam). Class: **regression**. Before this cutover, local gate calls ran on direct Anthropic, whose tenacity transport envelope (story arcticduck, `anthropic_model.py`) absorbed transient transport timeouts before they reached the gate. Switching the default gate provider to Bedrock removed that net without providing an equivalent gate-level degrade, so an exhausted transport timeout now escapes to the verdict-less fault. A reviewer of d2ce could plausibly have asked whether the Bedrock path had equivalent transient-timeout resilience — so it satisfies the "reviewer could have caught this" test.

**Divergence note (per protocol):** a whole-file blame of the *fix site* (`completion_recovery.py` / `completion_failures.py`) would misattribute to the banked-recovery story `9a08`/`dcc90`, which is the fix site, not the cause site (date test: `dcc90` 2026-07-27 predates the fault becoming reachable at `d2ce` 2026-08-04). `9a08` deliberately scoped recovery to *typed* exhaustion; it was `d2ce` that made the transport-timeout path escape verdict-less. Confidence **MODERATE**: the deeper "gate-level degrade for any transport failure" obligation was arguably never owned by a single ticket; `61d8` later added botocore retries to Bedrock (partial remediation) yet the fault persists, confirming the residual defect is at the decide-step/gate degrade layer. If one ticket must carry it, it is `d2ce`.

### Chronic-area context

Gate resilience here is demonstrably chronic (46a2→3211 "incomplete fix" tool-loop; 0707 banking follow-on defect; 12b7 sharding won't-fix; 10ae context rework; 61d8 inert Bedrock retry knobs; a live cluster of OPEN `llm-degrade` session_logs across all three gates). The recurring theme: **gates fail closed to an un-actionable "could not run" instead of degrading to a verdict.** This fix targets the transport-timeout instance of that theme.

### Fix direction (Phase 2)

Route an exhausted-provider `LLMUnavailableError` from the PRIMARY verify run into a **deterministic degrade** — finalize from the criterion bank via the existing no-LLM finalizer (honoring "can never die verdict-less"), *without* launching more (also-timing-out) LLM successor runs; when the bank is empty, emit a deterministic fail-closed verdict carrying a provider-unavailable finding. RED→GREEN with a held-out oracle + defect-seeded mutation.

comments.body:
## RCA — CORRECTED (supersedes the earlier comment; ultrathink + runtime experiments)

**Observed failure:** epic REB-3233 (3d7a-7795) close ran the completion verifier ~40 min, 3/3, then
faulted "completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict" with **exit 1** (hard,
non-retryable, offers `--force`).

**Earlier RCA framings were WRONG (recorded so they are not re-tried):**
- *"Missing degrade arm → fabricate a deterministic verdict"* — rejected: that verdict is
  `certifiable=False`; close_precheck.py:696-704 would then close the ticket WITHOUT a certified
  signature, violating the certified-close requirement and MASKING the real defect.
- *"600s per-call timeout too low for a large epic (scale it up)"* — rejected by runtime
  experiment: in a healthy Bedrock window the epic's converse calls run **~11s each**
  (`llm_ms 361s / 32 requests`), none near 600s, and the verify COMPLETES a `certifiable=true`
  PASS. So 600s is ample under normal conditions; the 3/3 ~40-min faults were a **sustained
  Bedrock-slowness window** (a transient provider availability event), not a structural >600s call.
- *caused_by = d2ce (Bedrock-default cutover)* — WITHDRAWN: the exit-1-vs-exit-11 defect is
  **provider-independent** (it drops the disposition for ANY retryable outage), so the Bedrock
  cutover is not its origin.

**PROVEN root cause (provider-independent, structural):** a retryable provider outage that occurs
MID-RUN in the completion gate surfaces as a **non-retryable exit-1 hard fault instead of the
exit-11 "transient — retry"** the gate posture was designed to produce.
- `close_precheck.py:629-631` is the exit-11 consumer: `_outcome = failure.outcome_of(exc);
  _rc = 11 if (_outcome and _outcome.retryable) else 1`.
- The classifier DOES compute the retryable disposition and attach it to the raised
  `LLMUnavailableError` (`run_failure.py:174 provider_err.outcome = outcome`).
- BUT the mid-run completion outage is stringified into a `RunResult.error` at the workflow-executor
  boundary (`executor.py` StepResult/RunResult carry `error: str`, not the exception), and
  `raise_completion_workflow_failure` (completion_failures.py:231 / the CompletionRecoveryError
  raises in completion_recovery.py) raises a **fresh `LLMError`/`CompletionRecoveryError` with NO
  `.outcome`** → `outcome_of(exc)` returns `None` → `_rc = 1`.
- **Parity proof:** the plan-review gate does NOT have this bug — `plan_review_recovery.py`
  `_degraded_plan_review_verdict` (story authorial-hated-blackbear) does
  `outcome = failure.outcome_of(error)` then `**failure.resolution_fields(outcome)` so a retryable
  outage maps to exit 11. The completion gate was left on "Shape B (raised error)" but its mid-run
  raise path never attaches `.outcome`.

**Discriminating evidence:**
- Healthy-window full epic verify (REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT=1200, 1 attempt): **COMPLETED, verdict PASS,
  certifiable=true**, 10 criteria, 32 requests, ~11s/call — disproves the "structural >600s" and
  "infra-broken" rivals and confirms the fault was a transient slowness window.
- Small-leaf Bedrock health probe: PASS certifiable=true in 140s — Bedrock healthy.
- Code trace: `failure.outcome_of` (failure.py:550) reads `getattr(error,"outcome",None)` — it does
  NOT re-classify; the raised error MUST carry `.outcome`, and the mid-run completion path does not.

**Defect attribution (caused_by = authorial-hated-blackbear / commit 3938c7ed2d60, epic jira-reb-687):**
that story ("two-scope gate posture — exit 11, disposition plumbing") built the exit-11 CONSUMER for
the completion gate (`_completion_precheck` raises 11 on a retryable `.outcome`) and wired the
PRODUCER for the plan-review/code-review "Shape A" degraded-verdict paths, but never wired the
completion gate's mid-run "Shape B" raise path to ATTACH `.outcome`. Consumer added, producer
omitted, within the one integrator story — an incomplete implementation of its own design. Class:
plan_defect. (Secondary: `failure._map` has an httpx-timeout retryable arm but no botocore arm — a
provider-parity gap that determines whether a Bedrock read-timeout is retryable at first
classification; folded into the fix for robustness.)

**Fix (mirror the blackbear plan-review pattern in the completion gate):** forward the retryable
disposition from the primary/recovery exception's `.outcome` onto the error raised by
`raise_completion_workflow_failure`, so `outcome_of(exc)` returns retryable and close_precheck exits
11 "transient — retry" (never uncertified-closes, never fabricates a verdict). Plus add the
botocore/provider-agnostic read-timeout arm to `failure._map` for parity with httpx.

## Context / Problem

Closing a large epic runs the completion-verifier close gate, whose final
`decide@then/verify` step makes an LLM (Bedrock `converse`) call. On epic
`3d7a-7795-efde-4df7` (REB-3233, 13 children) the gate ran ~40 minutes and then
FAULTED — it produced **neither PASS nor FAIL/BLOCK**, but an error:

```
cannot close 3d7a-7795-efde-4df7: completion verification could not run
(completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict:
 step 'decide@then/verify' failed: the LLM provider call failed:
 Read timeout on endpoint URL:
 "https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6/converse").
```

This is a fault in the gate itself: a transient/among-oversized provider Read
timeout is surfaced as "could not run / no verdict", so a legitimate close cannot
complete without `--force`. Reproduced deterministically: three consecutive close
attempts on this epic all faulted identically (~40+ min each, EXIT 1).

`src/rebar/llm/failure.py:271` classifies `httpx.ReadTimeout`
(`httpx.TimeoutException`) as `WAIT_AND_RETRY`, and `config.py` documents a retry
policy over transient timeouts — yet the gate still terminated with no verdict via
`completion_failures.py:232` ("... did not produce a verdict"). So either the
verifier's decide-step path does not apply the retry, retries are exhausted because
each attempt sends an oversized accumulated context that itself read-times-out, or
the effective per-request timeout is too low for a large-AC epic-close verification.

This defect class has rich history (verifier sharding `12b7`, banked/resumable AC
verification `2948`, context reworks `10ae`, step-budget loops `46a2`/`3211`,
`REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT` wiring `02cd`, Bedrock provider seam+timeout `061c`, gates
running minutes-scale `1e88`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A transient provider Read timeout during the completion verifier's
  `decide@then/verify` step no longer terminates the gate with "could not run / no
  verdict"; it is handled per the WAIT_AND_RETRY classification (bounded retry) OR
  the verification work is bounded so a single call cannot exceed the provider read
  timeout — root cause to be confirmed by /rebar-debug before the fix. Proven by a
  RED→GREEN test that exercises the confirmed mechanism.
- [x] A large-epic close (many children / large AC set) completes through the gate
  without a raw provider read-timeout fault, or degrades to an actionable verdict
  rather than an un-actionable "could not run".

## Testing

- [x] A unit/integration test reproduces the faulting path (verifier decide step
  raising `httpx.ReadTimeout`) and asserts the post-fix behavior (bounded retry
  and/or bounded context / actionable outcome), seen RED before the fix and GREEN
  after, with a mutation check.
compiled_state.title: Completion-verifier close gate faults (no verdict) on a Bedrock Read timeout during decide@then/verify for large-epic closes
